newsitem.title: FRANCE: Police find weapons cache in Corsica.
newsitem.headline: Police find weapons cache in Corsica.

text.p: Paramilitary police found several dozen handguns, rifles and rocket-launchers in Corsica on Friday as seven separatist sympathisers were brought before Paris anti-terrorism judges in another probe.
Gendarmerie police said the weapons cache was discovered in Borgo, south of the town of Bastia, in a probe following the machinegunning of gendarmerie barracks in Sainte Marie Sicche on December 27.
The arms including Remington rifles and ammunition were found at the home of one of nine suspects detained in the probe.
Separately, justice sources said seven men close to the A Cuncolta Naziunalista separatist movement were presented to anti-terrorism judges Jean-Francois Ricard and Laurence Le Vert in Paris.
A Cuncolta Naziunalista is the legal facade of the outlawed separatist Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC).
The seven are suspected of involvement in the machinegunning of the Le Pascal Paoli hotel in the town of Aregno in October. The FLNC has claimed responsibility for the attack.
Justice sources said the seven would likely be placed under investigation and ordered held in preventive custody.
Overnight, unidentified attackers blasted two post offices and a garage with small explosive charges on the French Mediterranean island, police said.
The attacks, in the villages of Furiani, Propriano and Olmeto, caused slight damage and no casualties. All the premises were empty at the time.

No one claimed responsibility for the attacks but they bore the hallmarks of Corsican separatist groups whom authorities hold responsible for many of the estimated 1,200 bomb blasts on the island in the past two years.
The bombings came a day after a member of an elite paramilitary police unit was shot and slightly wounded by a separatist in the north Corsica town of Bastia.
